title: Engine-enforced segregation of duties across financial processes
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Segregation of duties is enforced by the Unbound command engine, not by procedure. For posting-rule version approval, manual journals, bank and payee master changes, reconciliation sign-off, close certification and payment release, the approver must be a different principal from the preparer, and the check runs inside the command transaction (RR-UNB-ACC-022-r2, CNV-GOV-003). The rule applies to humans, service accounts and AI agents alike, so one actor cannot control request, approval and reconciliation (GOV-AUTH-004); AI can never approve its own accounting actions. Until a deterministic release gate is accepted by the sponsor's auditor and board, payment release requires three distinct people. Reconciliation sits outside the payment chain. Every conflict evaluation emits a DutyConflictEvaluated event (UNB-SCTRL-002) so an auditor can test the full population rather than a sample.
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Implement the SoD conflict matrix as a server-side policy evaluated in every consequential command; publish the matrix per sponsor; negative tests prove self-approval is denied.

Collusion between two authorized people is not prevented by SoD alone.

title: Approval limits and delegation of authority with aggregation
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Every approval is checked against a versioned delegation-of-authority (DoA) register. Each entry declares the decision type, per-item limit, cumulative limit, aggregation window and key (approver by counterparty), the board or officer resolution that grants it and an expiry (UNB-XIN-ERP-005). An approval above the per-item limit, or one that would push the approver's cumulative approvals to the same counterparty over the window limit, is rejected and escalated, which defeats invoice or grant splitting. Entries become invalid at the next check when the holder is inactive in the workforce feed or the source resolution is superseded. Grant approvals route by role, amount, risk, relationship and exception, with dual control where policy requires (RR-UNB-GRANT-012-r1).
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Build the DoA register and limit evaluator as a deterministic policy component; feed it from the sponsor's board resolutions and the workforce identity feed.

title: Change control over fee schedules, rates and fee computation
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Fees can only be charged under an approved, versioned fee schedule. Each version declares its basis, day count, accrual and settlement cadence, minimum and exactly one payer source; a schedule with a missing or ambiguous payer source cannot activate (CNV-FIN-002, UNB-XIN-ERP-002). Schedule publication is a high-risk policy change that requires dual control (UNB-RULE-020) and is effective-dated rather than edited in place, so fee computation segments at each version boundary (UNB-XIN-ERP-001). Fee runs are idempotent per fund, schedule, period and segment set and move through Accrued, Assessed and Posted; waivers are approved exceptions with expiry and corrections are compensating entries (RR-ADM-028-r1). Only the fee engine may emit authoritative fee events (UNB-XIN-ERP-007). Operator charges to a sponsor are billed from the operator's own system and never posted into a tenant ledger (UNB-XIN-ERP-003).
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Implement fee schedules as immutable versions with an activation gate, independent recomputation and a monthly fee reconciliation.

title: SOC 1 relevance and plan for customers' financial statement audits
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Where Echelon hosts or performs fund accounting, NAV or reconciliation for a sponsor it does not control, those processes are relevant to the sponsor's internal control over financial reporting. The requirement is a SOC 1 Type 2 report covering ledger posting, NAV and unitization, reconciliation, change management and logical access, obtained before the first such sponsor's fiscal year end, with a sponsor-specific list of complementary user entity controls (UNB-XIN-ACC-009, CNV-GOV-001). Before live reliance, the sponsor's external auditor's planned approach (rely on a SOC 1, test Unbound directly or test substantively) is recorded, and the control register tags each control with the report it supports (UNB-RCN-PLT-013). Today no SOC 1 or SOC 2 report exists and none is in progress.

intended_practice: Begin SOC 1 Type 2 readiness, including the first observation period, before the first staffed-administration client goes live (CNV-GOV-001); engage a CPA firm to confirm scope.

challenge.customer_intent: The sponsor's auditor needs a basis to rely on controls at the service organization that affect the sponsor's financial statements.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Auditor cannot rely on Unbound controls, increasing audit fees or producing control deficiencies at the sponsor.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: A SOC 1 Type 2 tests a sample of control operation over a period and is widely accepted, but its evidence is retrospective and sampled.
challenge.legally_required: Not by statute for nonprofit sponsors. For SEC-registrant customers, management's ICFR assessment under SOX 404 must address outsourced processes, which usually means a SOC 1.
challenge.contractually_required: Commonly required in service contracts and by user auditors; CNV-GOV-001 requires contracts to include right-to-audit and an evidence pack.
challenge.historical_convention: SOC 1 (formerly SAS 70) is the default reliance mechanism for outsourced accounting.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Not possible; reliance is an auditor judgment.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Engine-enforced controls (SoD, balanced journals, period locks) reduce the number of manual controls the report must cover.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Full-population, generated evidence with information-produced-by-entity support could let auditors test every instance rather than a sample.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Continuous population-level evidence plus a SOC 1 Type 2, rather than instead of one.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Only if the auditor validates the evidence-generating system (ITGCs and IPE); CNV-GOV-001 permits replacing manual procedures only after auditor confirmation.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Low as a replacement, high as a supplement.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Ineffective ITGCs or unvalidated report logic would make generated evidence unreliable.
challenge.conventional_cost: High: CPA fees and an observation period, recurring annually.
challenge.alternative_cost: Medium engineering cost to generate evidence; does not remove audit fees.
challenge.alternative_risks: Overclaiming that continuous evidence is equivalent to an attestation.
supporting_arguments: Population testing is technically stronger than sampling.
Generated evidence lowers recurring audit effort.
opposing_arguments: User auditors are bound by professional standards that assume a service auditor's report or direct testing.
A new vendor with no operating history is unlikely to be trusted without an attestation.

title: Internal control framework, control register and control state honesty
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Unbound's financial controls are organized around a COSO-aligned control register in which every control has a unique ID, owner, objective, risk, trigger, evidence schema, source system, reviewer and failure behavior (SOC2-001, TVR-CMP-001). The register separates Proposed, Designed, Implemented, Operating, Tested, Deficient, Remediating and AuditorReviewed and never infers one state from another (SOC2-019). Today all 90 UNB-CTRL controls in the master matrix are Designed only, with no operating evidence, test execution or auditor review. Every material capability has exactly one accountable human role even when execution is automated (UNB-CTL-003).

intended_practice: Operate the register as data that generates customer answers, so a status can only advance with attached evidence.

title: Management review controls and reliability of information used in review
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Management review controls in Unbound operate on reports whose completeness and accuracy can be proven. Every financial report, statement and dashboard figure is computed from a sealed financial snapshot identified by sponsor entity, period or as-of instant and ledger commit watermark, so recomputation yields identical figures (UNB-XIN-EVA-003). Generated reports carry information-produced-by-entity support: query definition, parameters, population counts, hash and run log (CNV-GOV-001). The controller signs off reconciliation completeness monthly (CNV-FIN-004), review sign-offs and exceptions are evidence events (UNB-CTRL-045, UNB-CTRL-048), and control owners attest periodically while independent reviewers challenge completeness (SOC2-024). Manual review is replaced by generated evidence only after the auditor confirms reliance.

intended_practice: Generate IPE packages automatically with each review report and record reviewer, precision threshold and follow-up in the evidence store.

challenge.customer_intent: Ensure a knowledgeable person reviews financial results with enough precision to catch material errors.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Material misstatement passes review because the reviewer looked at incomplete or wrong data or reviewed superficially.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Management review controls are frequently cited by auditors as insufficiently precise or lacking evidence of what was reviewed.
challenge.contractually_required: Implicitly, through SOC 1 control objectives and sponsor audit expectations.
challenge.historical_convention: Signed review checklists and email approvals.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Partially: reproducible sealed snapshots eliminate the data-completeness question for review inputs.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: Deterministic exception rules (breaks, thresholds, aging) can flag every item that exceeds precision, leaving humans to judge exceptions.
challenge.continuous_evidence: IPE metadata and sign-off events per report.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Rule-based exception detection on the full population plus human review of exceptions and of the rules themselves.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, if rule versions, thresholds and outputs are retained and the auditor validates the rules.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Moderate; auditors accept exception-based review when thresholds are documented and IPE is supported.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Rules that are not independently approved or thresholds loosened without second approval (RR-UNB-ACC-018-r1).
challenge.conventional_cost: Low tooling cost, high recurring staff time.
challenge.alternative_risks: Reviewers may rubber-stamp clean exception reports; judgment-only risks (estimates, classifications) are not rule-detectable.
opposing_arguments: Some reviews require judgment that rules cannot encode.
Auditors still need evidence the reviewer understood and investigated exceptions.

title: Automation, AI and deterministic rules within financial controls
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Unbound classifies every decision as deterministic (D), probabilistic recommendation or flag (P) or human-authorized (H); a probabilistic output alone can never clear a control or move money (UNB-CTL-001). AI may propose journal drafts and classifications but cannot bypass posting, approval or reconciliation controls (UNB-ACC-029); state-changing events with financial consequences come only from approved deterministic rules or authorized people (UNB-EVT-005); model-only auto-clear designs are prohibited (UNB-CTL-005). A deterministic release gate counts as an approver only when it runs a published, independently approved policy version, the human approvers cannot author or deploy it, ITGCs are effective and the auditor and board have accepted the design (CNV-GOV-003). Changes to control-relevant modules need two approvers, neither the author, and signed builds (CNV-PLT-010).

intended_practice: Encode D/P/H classification in the command catalog; agent principals can write only to an AI observation store (UNB-XIN-EVA-016).

challenge.customer_intent: Ensure no automated process can move money or alter books without accountable human authority.
challenge.adverse_outcome: Defective or manipulated automation releases funds or posts entries at scale.
challenge.conventional_control_effectiveness: Human dual approval is familiar but degrades with volume (approval fatigue) and is weak against well-crafted fraud.
challenge.legally_required: No statute requires a human approver for each payment; sponsor boards and auditors decide.
challenge.contractually_required: Bank agreements and sponsor policies commonly require dual control on release.
challenge.historical_convention: Two human approvals in a bank portal.
challenge.architectural_elimination: Agents have no write path to authoritative tables (UNB-XIN-EVA-016), which removes direct AI posting within that scope.
challenge.automatic_enforcement: An independently approved deterministic gate applies the same policy to every item without fatigue.
challenge.continuous_evidence: Gate version, inputs and decision for each item.
challenge.stronger_alternative: Deterministic gate as one approver plus human approval for exceptions and above-threshold items, with change control on the gate stronger than on any single approval.
challenge.alternative_verifiable: Yes, through ITGC testing of the gate and its change control, which CNV-GOV-003 makes a precondition.
challenge.customer_acceptance_likelihood: Uncertain; depends on each sponsor's auditor and board.
challenge.invalidating_conditions: Ineffective change management over the gate, or approvers able to influence gate policy.
challenge.conventional_cost: High recurring staff time, especially at year-end surge.
challenge.alternative_cost: Medium build plus ITGC assurance cost.
challenge.alternative_risks: A single defect affects every item; correlated failure.
supporting_arguments: CNV-GOV-003 keeps three-person release until acceptance.
opposing_arguments: Auditors may view an automated approver as a single point of failure.
Board members may expect a named person to approve each disbursement.

title: Exceptions, overrides, emergency access and compensating controls
status_rationale: Unbound requirements specify this design but nothing is implemented, operated or tested (unbound@9b38de47). The evidence mechanism, freshness and automation fields describe the target design.
target_answer: Exceptions to financial controls are explicit records with risk acceptance authority, expiry, compensating controls and follow-up (SOC2-033). Break-glass access uses sealed credentials outside the workforce IdP, needs two-person activation, expires within four hours and cannot perform domain transitions such as grant approval, payee change, ledger posting or hold removal (UNB-XIN-IAM-005). Any platform hold executes a sponsor-adopted policy, is time-bounded and never moves funds (CNV-PLT-007). Where a sponsor lacks staff for full SoD, enforced leave applies when two trained staff exist and anomaly analytics otherwise; each alternative control is documented with expiry (CNV-GOV-003, TVR-SEC-006). Any authoritative state change without a matching command event blocks affected payments until reviewed.
current_practice: Not established. Unbound exists only as requirements (unbound@9b38de47); there is no ledger, payment, workflow or control implementation, no production deployment and no customer. Unknown; no operating evidence located.
intended_practice: Implement the exception register and break-glass workflow, and run cross-role anomaly analytics for small-staff sponsors.
